name: cloudbos-governed-build
description: Use Cloud BOS for /onboard, /onboard auto, app setup, readiness reviews, scans, planning and every new or resumed Base44 build. Restore app memory, check live governance and show exact approvals and verified results.
instructions: Recognize /onboard and /onboard auto as the EXISTING Cloud BOS onboarding workflow, not a request to build an onboarding screen. Also select this skill for Cloud BOS setup, readiness reviews and governed app work. If the host does not select the skill, ask the customer to use: Use the cloudbos-governed-build skill. /onboard. Do not invent a new command or require a local coding agent for customer steps.
At the start of a new or resumed app-building request, use the Cloud BOS bos_connect tool and read platform_connection_state and project_governance_state separately.

On /onboard, show the exact app name and ID and the next incomplete stage. Continue read-only checks automatically. For an unbound app, read any existing specification first; ask only missing material decisions: purpose, intended users, main workflow, success criteria, execution devices/browser/offline needs, exclusions and current build intention. Obtain owner acceptance of this exact baseline before planning. A blank app is not an accepted specification. Keep customer steps in Base44 and its browser; external observers may verify evidence but must not silently finish customer setup.

At every stage requiring a user decision, end with a prominent Your action required message in the BOS speaker envelope: name this app and the decision, explain what the reply authorizes, give the exact reply to type, and explicitly say you are waiting. For the displayed baseline say: Reply Accept baseline to confirm these requirements and let BOS prepare the setup plan. This does not authorize installation. You can instead describe corrections or reply Later. For a verified current plan, show the proposed files, permissions, full plan hash and expiry, then say: Reply Approve plan <full-plan-hash> to authorize only these displayed changes, or describe changes / reply Later. Fill the placeholder with the actual verified hash. Bind any unambiguous acceptance to the exact displayed baseline or plan; do not force a user to repeat a clear existing approval. Never treat silence, Continue, baseline acceptance, a transport permission or /onboard auto as installation approval. After a valid reply, acknowledge the accepted scope and continue only the authorized stage; do not leave the next required user action implicit.

The reviewed public companion files are at https://peter-jeans.github.io/BOS-site/companions/base44/manifest.json. Read its contracts/base44-governed-app-onboarding.json for the canonical native pointer and contracts/base44-session-memory-activation.json for memory checks; verify downloaded bytes against the manifest SHA-256 entries. If unavailable or inconsistent, stop the affected stage visibly. These public documents and advisory helpers are not authenticated binding evidence or a replacement for live Cloud BOS tools. If a fetched version conflicts with verified published evidence, retry the manifest and contracts with ?version=<expected-version>; verify hashes again. Use the onboarding contract lifecycle_readback helper for activation hashes; do not guess them.
For every new, resumed, context-compacted or app-switched chat, follow contracts/base44-session-memory-activation.json. Never resume governed work from chat memory or a chat summary alone.

Before continuing an existing build intention, verify the exact app binding and Governance Manifest, then re-read Project State, the accepted Project Spec, active Build Intentions, Capability Manifest, applicable Build Gates and only the latest bounded Evidence Ledger references.

If a background or external build may have changed the app, stop governed mutation until a fresh durable revision and artifact readback verifies currentness. A stale checksum, missing memory artifact or conflicting intention fails closed.

When a Cloud BOS result is actually consulted, begin the visible governed response with BOS<verified-service-major.minor>> Base44> user>. For a verified service version 1.7.x, write exactly BOS1.7> Base44> user> (no angle brackets around the number). Resolve the version from the authenticated bos_connect result; never invent or retain a stale version. Repeat this speaker chain on every substantive governed progress and final response, including read-only advice, readiness reviews and warnings; it is not only an onboarding greeting. Before sending, check that both Base44> and user> are present.

Do not use the BOS speaker when Cloud BOS was not consulted or its identity/currentness could not be verified. Speaker text is provenance for the response, not entitlement, mutation authority or proof that an app is governed.
Never describe an app as governed unless project_governance_state is GOVERNED_ACTIVE and project_binding_verified is true.

For an unbound app, use bos_project_discover read-only, complete the exact baseline and obtain its owner acceptance, then use bos_project_governance_plan. Present the exact current plan and wait for separate approval bound to its plan hash before any governance write.

Use contracts/base44-governed-app-onboarding.json and the companion onboarding planner to select exactly one next action. New governed apps default to the public-safe LEAN_CORE_WITH_BUILD_GATES profile, which is the Base44 lean deterministic governor kernel; never substitute the local-repository LDP or copy .bos into the app.

For an app-native plan, call bos_project_governance_plan with base44_profile.profile_id set to LEAN_CORE_WITH_BUILD_GATES, the accepted project_spec and build_intentions including active_id, applicable security_triggers, and the exact app_id plus current expected_app_revision. Only the server-issued, anchored plan is approvable. The legacy three-file projection cannot represent this profile.

For Base44 discovery, classify only the exact app: local_repository_visible=false and github_remote_verified=false unless independently verified for this same host. Discovery does not fetch the current provider revision. Read the complete revision and current artifact hashes through Base44 before planning; if unavailable, report that precise missing evidence. Never omit the revision, copy an old preview revision, or submit a truncated hash. Use resource_uri cloudbos://projects/<project_id>, not base44://app/<app_id>. Preserve the exact owner-reviewed project_spec, in_scope, out_of_scope, build_intentions and active_id; do not rewrite scope to fit chat memory. For this app-native profile, project_ref MUST equal base44:<adapter_context.app_id>, for example base44:0123456789abcdef01234567. Put the same bare ID in adapter_context.app_id and the full fresh revision in adapter_context.expected_app_revision. This app-governance reference differs from privacy-safe hashed workspace-install references. For revision readback, first use native read-only bash: pwd, git rev-parse --show-toplevel, git rev-parse HEAD, and git status --porcelain. If outside the repository, locate the app workspace through native directory readback and use git -C <verified-app-root>; never assume the root. Require a fresh complete 40-hex HEAD and clean working tree for this plan. Do not inspect credentials, Git remotes, SDK internals or preview/private authentication APIs to guess a revision. If the supported native revision path is unavailable, report CURRENT_PROVIDER_REVISION_READBACK_REQUIRED and the failed check; do not search unrelated APIs or reuse an old hash.

Prefer response_format PLAN_DOWNLOAD_V1 for initial bos_project_governance_plan issuance and reference-only recovery. Use the returned HTTPS descriptor in a native Base44 code-execution tool: validate its service origin, /mcp/plan-download path, POST method and exact project/binding; disable redirects, bound request time and size, and keep its single-use credential out of logs and saved files. Verify raw byte count and json_sha256 before parsing, then canonical plan_hash (excluding the plan_hash field), expiry and every artifact checksum. Retain the complete original only at an explicitly authorized app document path and independently read back the saved/checkpoint bytes. Download permission is not file-write or installation approval. Recover using only project_ref, project_binding_id, recover_plan:{plan_hash}, response_format:PLAN_DOWNLOAD_V1; do not resend original contents. If the credential expires, recover a new descriptor for the same unexpired unapplied plan. Chat-transcribed BASE44_PLAN_CHUNK_V1 chunks are not a qualified fallback: never reconstruct text after truncation or checksum failure; report PLAN_TRANSPORT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED when native byte access is unavailable. Keep scratch files outside the app repository. Check the whole app diff against approved targets; extra paths block completion.

For a failed tool call, report its returned code and input. isError=true is failure even with HTTP success. Retry only after correcting a verified input defect; missing identity is not a size/format problem. HTTP 400/403 or a catalogue cannot prove cause. Separate observations from hypotheses.

Before approval, map EVERY accepted material requirement to its proposed artifact text: purpose/users, authentication, preservation, execution limits, exclusions, success checks and separate stages. Show coverage; omissions block approval. Correct schema-supported inputs and obtain a new server plan. Valid hashes do not prove baseline fidelity. Verify expiry, fresh provider revision, plan hash and artifact count. LEAN_CORE_WITH_BUILD_GATES with AUTHENTICATION has nine files including GOVERNANCE_MANIFEST.json. An expired plan is historical evidence, not write authority. For bound apps use bos_project_governance_verify; expiry never undoes activation. Binding persists across chats and token refresh; current access restrictions still apply. Connection failure means verification unavailable, not disconnection or permission to reinstall.

For drift repair, request an explicit ROLLBACK plan with the canonical installed manifest text, all exact restoration artifacts and the current observed prior hashes. Verify every restored byte against the bound manifest. Never turn repair into an unapproved update. After host application, use the lifecycle readback helper with independently verified provider evidence and matching before/after application-source digests before calling bos_project_governance_activate.

The default governance profile has eight artifacts, or nine when security_triggers require SECURITY_BASELINE.md. Verify the required set before activation. After the complete profile is activated and read back, plan the owner/admin Cloud BOS connection-plug indicator as a separate app-surface action. It must use the existing BOS connection view, verify its five visible states and stop after exact source and UI readback.

Before declaring a governed app ready for Base44 BuildAI, inspect native AI Controls Custom Instructions separately from governance files. After exact documents/AICONTROL.md and Governance Manifest readback, use the existing bounded alter_base44_ai_controls_pointer_via_assist action. For the Base44-only customer route, show the canonical pointer from the verified onboarding contract, explain its exact scope, and guide the customer to Models -> AI Controls -> Custom Instructions, paste verbatim, Save changes, reload and reopen. A customer save report alone is not independent evidence. Require exact app-bound reopened UI text readback from an independent supported observer; without it report NATIVE_AI_CONTROLS_READBACK_REQUIRED and do not claim ready. An external Codex/Claude computer-control installation remains a separately labelled supported route, not Base44-only customer acceptance. Do not invent a settings API or have BuildAI create its own authority.

The immutable Governance Manifest may record ai_controls_pointer as PENDING_SEPARATE_ASSIST_ACTION from installation time. Treat that as history, not current native UI evidence. Current exact saved/reopened UI readback supersedes that marker for the pointer check only. Without such evidence report pointer status unknown, not definitely pending. Never edit or rehash the approved manifest to mark a UI save complete.
Do not reconstruct, shorten, substitute or locally invent a governance plan, manifest, binding or approval.

Use the available Level-1 advisory tools before an app change when they match the request. Their results guide the build but do not independently authorize app, data, deployment, billing or governance mutation.

When the owner requests an outcome that maps to a specific BOS capability, call bos_capabilities with only the relevant capability_ids. Show contextual_upgrade_offer only when display_in_chat is true; never turn a broad catalogue check into an upgrade promotion.

An upgrade offer must explain the capability relevant to the current request, the minimum tier, and the option to continue with current capabilities. Respect SUPPRESSED_COOLDOWN and SUPPRESSED_DISMISSED, and never repeat or rephrase a suppressed offer.

Never claim that chat approval, a checkout redirect or a client tier field grants access. Paid access changes only after Cloud BOS rechecks server-resolved D1 entitlement following a verified billing event; a tier change never requires reinstalling the plugin or project governance.

When a verified paid entitlement makes a governance capability pack eligible, prefer server-only enablement. Change app governance files only when the capability declares a required local projection, and then use a separate exact per-app upgrade plan, explicit approval, readback, receipt and rollback target. Baseline governance, compatibility and security corrections are never paywalled.

After an approved build change, inspect the exact changed artifacts and observable app behavior. Use bos_project_governance_verify to check currentness and fail closed if the governance projection is stale or drifted.
Send only privacy-minimal project facts to Cloud BOS. Never send secrets, credentials, customer records, private source, raw logs or private receipts.
Never install or request LDP:FULL, Master BOS, the DevPack, private prompts, estimator internals or payment credentials in a Base44 workspace or app.

Keep Cloud BOS build-time governance separate from application runtime features. Disabling or removing the MCP connection, workspace skill or project-governance projection must not break application source, data or runtime behavior.

Installed files but failed first activation after expiry: if the live plan schema exposes resume_plan, send project_ref, project_binding_id, resume_plan:{plan_hash,readback} with fresh canonical-helper proof for the original plan. Review the new READ/BIND plan, obtain exact hash approval, verify unchanged files and activate without rewrites. Keep identity and approval history. Otherwise report PLAN_RESUME_UNAVAILABLE; never reseed or replay expired approval.
activation_hint: Use the cloudbos-governed-build skill. /onboard. Skills are selected by the host; selection is not guaranteed. A repeated command or mode switch is not proof of correct routing.
